triage.reason: Common symptom-based presentation with clear diagnostic workup distinguishing stress, urge and overflow incontinence; strong interview and exam case.

demographics: More common in women overall, largely because of pregnancy, vaginal childbirth and menopause
Prevalence rises steadily with age in both sexes
Overflow incontinence is more common in men, usually related to prostate enlargement
More common in people with obesity and in current smokers

risk_factors.text: Female sex, especially after pregnancy, vaginal delivery or menopause
Older age with weakening of pelvic floor and bladder muscles
Prostate enlargement or prior prostate surgery in men
Neurologic disease such as multiple sclerosis, stroke or spinal cord injury
Congenital abnormality of the urinary tract

comorbidities: Multiple sclerosis or other neurologic disease
family_history: Urinary incontinence in a mother or sister
Bedwetting in childhood in the patient or a parent
social_history: Limited mobility or difficulty reaching a toilet

chief_complaints.text: I leak urine when I don't mean to
I can't make it to the bathroom in time
I have to wear a pad every day

hpi.onset: Gradual over months to years; often noticed after childbirth, weight gain, menopause or prostate problems
hpi.duration: Usually months to years by the time the patient seeks care
hpi.progression: Slowly worsens over time; may fluctuate with fluid intake, caffeine, activity and weight
hpi.location: Bladder and urethra; leakage felt at the opening of the urethra
hpi.quality: Involuntary loss of urine; stress type leaks in small spurts with pressure, urge type leaks in larger amounts with a sudden need to go, overflow type is a constant dribble
hpi.severity: Mild to moderate for most; can be severe enough to limit work, exercise and social life
hpi.timing: Stress type with coughing, sneezing, laughing, lifting or exercise; urge type with sudden urgency day or night; overflow type continuous dribbling
aggravating: Full bladder or rushing to the toilet
relieving: Emptying the bladder on a schedule
Wearing a pad or protective underwear
Crossing legs or sitting down when the urge hits

associated_symptoms.text: Going to the bathroom often during the day
Waking up at night to urinate
Feeling that the bladder is not completely empty
Needing to urinate again soon after finishing
Avoiding activities because of fear of leaking

pertinent_negatives: Sudden inability to urinate at all
New numbness, weakness or trouble walking

positives.text: Leaking urine with coughing, sneezing or lifting
Sudden urge to urinate with leakage before reaching the toilet
Getting up at night to urinate
Weak urinary stream or dribbling after urination
Numbness or tingling in the legs or feet

negatives: Loss of sensation in the saddle area

positives.text: Embarrassment or worry about leaking in public

argues_against: Major depression as the primary cause
Colorectal cancer or severe bowel disease

atypical.how_it_differs: Leakage may be mixed or functional rather than a single type, and is often accompanied by mobility problems, cognitive impairment or medication effects.
Stress leakage is common in late pregnancy and after delivery because of pelvic floor pressure and stretching; it often improves in the months after birth.
Increased abdominal pressure worsens stress leakage, and symptoms often improve with weight loss.
Can cause both urge leakage from bladder nerve damage and overflow leakage from incomplete bladder emptying; high blood sugar also increases urine volume.
Daytime or nighttime wetting is common and usually reflects delayed bladder control rather than adult-type incontinence; it is more common in boys and when a parent had the same problem.
missing_classic_features: Adult pattern of stress or urge leakage

general.mild: Comfortable, well-groomed, no distress; may mention needing a bathroom soon
general.moderate: Mild embarrassment or anxiety when discussing leakage; may wear a pad or protective underwear
general.severe: Reluctant to sit through a long exam; may smell of urine; visibly distressed about leakage
general.critical: Not applicable; urinary incontinence itself is not a critical illness, though a patient with acute retention or cord compression would appear uncomfortable or toxic

findings.maneuver: With a comfortably full bladder, ask the patient to cough forcefully while you observe the urethral meatus
findings.finding: Immediate small spurt of urine from the urethra with the cough

findings.maneuver: Ask the patient to run water or imagine running water while observing for leakage
findings.finding: Leakage of urine with a sudden urge before reaching the toilet

findings.maneuver: Observe the urethral meatus for a minute after the patient finishes voiding
findings.finding: Continuous or intermittent dribbling of urine after voiding

findings.maneuver: Palpate the suprapubic area and percuss for a distended bladder
findings.finding: A firm, dull, palpable bladder above the pubic symphysis, suggesting incomplete emptying or retention

findings.maneuver: Inspect the vulva and vagina and perform a speculum exam if indicated
findings.finding: Thin, pale, dry vaginal mucosa with loss of rugae, consistent with genitourinary syndrome of menopause

findings.maneuver: Ask the patient to bear down while you inspect the introitus and perform a bimanual exam
findings.finding: Descent of the bladder, uterus or rectum toward or through the introitus

findings.maneuver: Ask the patient to squeeze the pelvic floor muscles around your examining finger
findings.finding: Weak or absent voluntary pelvic floor contraction

findings.maneuver: Perform a digital rectal exam to assess prostate size, nodules and sphincter tone
findings.finding: Enlarged, smooth, non-nodular prostate with preserved median sulcus, consistent with benign prostatic hyperplasia

findings.maneuver: Test lower extremity strength, sensation, reflexes, perineal sensation and anal sphincter tone
findings.finding: Normal strength, sensation, reflexes and sphincter tone

findings.maneuver: Measure temperature and inspect for systemic signs of infection

labs.caveat: Positive leukocyte esterase with nitrite and bacteriuria suggests a urinary tract infection as a transient cause of urgency and leakage; treat and reassess before labeling chronic incontinence.
Supports a urinary tract infection, a reversible cause of urge leakage.
Pyuria points to infection or inflammation rather than to the incontinence itself.
Microscopic hematuria without infection needs evaluation for stone or urothelial tumor; it is not explained by uncomplicated incontinence.
Hyperglycemia causes osmotic diuresis and can worsen both urgency and overflow leakage.
Screens for undiagnosed diabetes, a treatable contributor.
A rising creatinine suggests obstructive uropathy or chronic kidney disease from incomplete bladder emptying; check a postvoid residual.
Rises with dehydration or obstructive uropathy.
Negative. Check in anyone who could be pregnant before imaging or starting medication.
Leukocytosis is not expected from incontinence itself; it suggests pyelonephritis or another infection.

imaging.preferred_when: First-line when incomplete emptying or overflow incontinence is suspected

findings.text: Elevated postvoid residual volume, typically over 100–150 mL, indicating incomplete bladder emptying
Normal postvoid residual, supporting stress or urge incontinence rather than overflow
Distended bladder with a large retained volume
Bladder diverticulum or trabeculated wall from chronic outlet obstruction

imaging.preferred_when: Suspected obstruction, incomplete emptying or renal impairment

findings.text: Hydronephrosis from chronic bladder outlet obstruction or high postvoid residual

imaging.study: CT abdomen and pelvis without contrast
imaging.preferred_when: Suspected stone, mass or anatomic abnormality not seen on ultrasound
Suspected cord compression or cauda equina syndrome

findings.text: Disc herniation, mass or compression of the cauda equina
Usually nonspecific; occasionally a radiopaque stone or fecal loading

initial.why: Screens for infection, hematuria and glucosuria as reversible causes of leakage
Assesses renal function and looks for a high BUN/creatinine pattern of obstruction or dehydration
Hyperglycemia causes osmotic diuresis and worsens urgency and overflow
Distinguishes overflow incontinence from stress or urge incontinence and guides management
Rules out pregnancy before imaging or medication

confirmatory.why: Defines the type of incontinence when the diagnosis is unclear or surgery is being considered
confirmatory.only_if: Defines the type of incontinence when the diagnosis is unclear or surgery is being considered

confirmatory.why: Evaluates the bladder and urethra for stone, tumor or stricture
confirmatory.only_if: hematuria, recurrent infection or suspected anatomic abnormality

supporting.why: Screens for undiagnosed diabetes contributing to symptoms

supporting.only_if: renal impairment, recurrent infection or suspected obstruction

supporting.test: CT abdomen and pelvis without contrast
supporting.only_if: hematuria or suspected anatomic abnormality not seen on ultrasound

supporting.why: Evaluates for cord compression or cauda equina syndrome
supporting.only_if: new neurologic deficits, saddle anesthesia or bowel incontinence

not_indicated.why: Not routinely needed unless infection or systemic illness is suspected
No role in the routine evaluation of incontinence
No role in the routine evaluation of incontinence

not_indicated.test: ct abdomen and pelvis without contrast
not_indicated.why: Not first-line; reserve for suspected stone or mass
not_indicated.only_if: hematuria or suspected anatomic abnormality not seen on ultrasound

not_indicated.why: Not routine; reserve for suspected cord compression
not_indicated.only_if: new neurologic deficits, saddle anesthesia or bowel incontinence

not_indicated.why: Not routine; reserve for hematuria, recurrent infection or suspected anatomic abnormality
not_indicated.only_if: hematuria, recurrent infection or suspected anatomic abnormality

not_indicated.why: Not routine; reserve for unclear diagnosis or surgical planning
not_indicated.only_if: diagnosis is unclear or surgery is being considered

decision_points: Check a postvoid residual before treating urge symptoms; a high residual changes the diagnosis to overflow and makes anticholinergics unsafe
Treat urinary tract infection first and reassess; infection can cause transient urgency and leakage
Pregnancy test before imaging or starting medication in anyone who could be pregnant
New neurologic deficits, saddle anesthesia or bowel incontinence require urgent spinal imaging for cauda equina syndrome

differential.name: Urinary tract infection
differential.why_considered: Infection causes urgency, frequency and leakage that can look like urge incontinence
differential.trigger: Dysuria, fever or new-onset urgency in a patient without a prior leakage pattern

history: Sudden onset over days rather than months
labs: Positive leukocyte esterase and nitrite on urinalysis
imaging: Not routinely needed; ultrasound or CT reserved for suspected obstruction or abscess

differential.name: Overactive bladder
differential.why_considered: Urgency and frequency are the core symptoms of both urge incontinence and overactive bladder

history: Symptoms controlled by bladder training and antimuscarinics
imaging: Normal bladder ultrasound with low postvoid residual

differential.name: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
differential.why_considered: Enlarged prostate causes incomplete emptying, dribbling and overflow leakage in men

exam: Enlarged, smooth, non-nodular prostate on digital rectal exam
imaging: Elevated postvoid residual on bladder ultrasound
Hydronephrosis on renal ultrasound in chronic obstruction

differential.name: Cauda equina syndrome
differential.why_considered: Nerve compression can cause loss of bladder control along with neurologic deficits
differential.trigger: New saddle numbness, leg weakness or bowel incontinence with urinary leakage

history: Sudden onset of urinary retention or overflow leakage
labs: Not diagnostic; urgent imaging is the priority
imaging: MRI lumbar spine showing disc herniation, mass or compression of the cauda equina

differential.name: Bladder or urothelial cancer
differential.why_considered: A bladder tumor can cause urgency, frequency and leakage, and may present with hematuria
differential.trigger: Gross or microscopic hematuria, especially in a smoker or older adult

history: Irritative voiding symptoms that do not respond to usual therapy
exam: Usually normal; may have a palpable pelvic mass in advanced disease
imaging: Bladder mass on ultrasound or CT urography

differential.name: Fecal impaction
differential.why_considered: A loaded rectum can press on the bladder and cause urgency, frequency and overflow leakage

exam: Hard stool palpable on rectal exam

differential.name: Diabetes mellitus
differential.why_considered: Hyperglycemia causes osmotic diuresis and nerve damage that can produce urgency and overflow leakage

history: Symptoms worsen with poor glycemic control
labs: Elevated fasting glucose or hemoglobin A1c
imaging: Not diagnostic; bladder ultrasound may show elevated postvoid residual

severity.mild: Occasional small leaks with strong triggers such as coughing or heavy lifting; no pads or only rare pad use; does not limit daily activities
severity.moderate: Regular leakage requiring daily pads; avoids some activities or plans routes around bathrooms; quality of life noticeably affected
severity.severe: Frequent or continuous leakage requiring protective garments; withdraws from work, exercise and social life; skin irritation or recurrent urinary tract infections may develop
severity.critical: Not applicable; urinary incontinence itself is not life-threatening, but acute urinary retention with overflow or cauda equina syndrome requires urgent evaluation

red_flags.finding: Gross hematuria or persistent microscopic hematuria
red_flags.meaning: Needs evaluation for bladder or urothelial cancer, stone or other structural lesion

red_flags.finding: New saddle anesthesia, leg weakness or bowel incontinence
red_flags.meaning: Possible cauda equina syndrome; obtain urgent MRI
Suggests urinary tract infection or pyelonephritis rather than uncomplicated incontinence

red_flags.finding: Sudden inability to urinate with a palpable bladder
red_flags.meaning: Acute urinary retention; requires immediate bladder decompression

red_flags.finding: Leakage that is new and severe in an older adult with confusion
red_flags.meaning: Consider infection, medication effect or neurologic event rather than chronic incontinence

complications.name: Skin breakdown and dermatitis
clues: Chronic dampness in the perineal area

complications.name: Recurrent urinary tract infection
clues: Repeated dysuria and positive urine cultures

complications.name: Social isolation and depression
clues: Low mood or loss of interest

complications.name: Falls and fractures
clues: Rushing to the bathroom at night

special_populations.differences: Leakage is often mixed or functional, worsened by mobility problems, cognitive impairment and medications; assess for reversible causes and fall risk.
Stress leakage is common in late pregnancy and after delivery from pelvic floor pressure and stretching; it often improves in the months after birth, and pelvic floor exercises are first-line.
Increased abdominal pressure worsens stress leakage; weight loss can reduce symptoms and is a key part of management.
Can cause urge leakage from bladder neuropathy and overflow leakage from incomplete emptying; hyperglycemia also increases urine volume and worsens symptoms.

Daytime or nighttime wetting usually reflects delayed bladder control rather than adult-type incontinence; it is more common in boys and when a parent had the same problem, and most children outgrow it.

key_questions.question: Can you describe exactly when you leak urine?
key_questions.looking_for: Leakage with coughing, sneezing, laughing or lifting points to stress incontinence; leakage after a sudden strong urge points to urge incontinence; continuous dribbling points to overflow

key_questions.question: Do you leak before you can reach the toilet after a sudden urge to go?
key_questions.looking_for: A sudden, uncontrollable urge with leakage before reaching the toilet suggests urge incontinence or overactive bladder

key_questions.question: How much urine leaks each time, and how often?
key_questions.looking_for: Small spurts with activity suggest stress; larger volumes with urgency suggest urge; constant dribbling suggests overflow

key_questions.question: Do you feel like your bladder is not completely empty after you urinate?
key_questions.looking_for: Incomplete emptying suggests overflow incontinence and should prompt a postvoid residual check

key_questions.question: How many times do you urinate during the day and at night?
key_questions.looking_for: Frequency and nocturia support urge incontinence or overactive bladder

key_questions.question: Do you use pads or protective underwear, and how many per day?
key_questions.looking_for: Quantifies severity and impact on daily life

key_questions.question: Does it burn or hurt when you urinate, or have you had fever or chills?
key_questions.looking_for: Dysuria, fever or chills suggest a urinary tract infection as a reversible cause of urgency and leakage

key_questions.question: Have you seen blood in your urine?
key_questions.looking_for: Gross or microscopic hematuria requires evaluation for bladder or urothelial cancer, stone or other structural lesion

key_questions.question: Have you had any new numbness in the saddle area, leg weakness or loss of bowel control?
key_questions.looking_for: Saddle anesthesia, leg weakness or bowel incontinence suggests cauda equina syndrome and needs urgent MRI

key_questions.question: Have you been unable to urinate at all, or do you feel a constant need to go with a very full bladder?
key_questions.looking_for: Acute urinary retention with a palpable bladder requires immediate decompression

key_questions.question: How many pregnancies and vaginal deliveries have you had?
key_questions.looking_for: Multiple vaginal deliveries increase risk of pelvic floor weakness and stress incontinence

key_questions.question: Have you gone through menopause?
key_questions.looking_for: Menopause with genitourinary syndrome of menopause contributes to stress and urge symptoms

key_questions.question: Have you had prostate surgery or problems with your prostate?
key_questions.looking_for: Prostate enlargement or prior prostate surgery in men suggests overflow incontinence or sphincter injury

key_questions.question: Do you have diabetes, multiple sclerosis, stroke or a spinal cord injury?
key_questions.looking_for: Neurologic disease or diabetes can cause urge or overflow incontinence from bladder neuropathy

key_questions.question: What medicines do you take, including diuretics, sedatives or bladder medicines?
key_questions.looking_for: Diuretics, sedatives, anticholinergics and alpha-blockers can worsen or cause leakage

key_questions.question: How much caffeine and alcohol do you drink each day?
key_questions.looking_for: High caffeine or alcohol intake can worsen urgency and frequency

key_questions.question: Do you smoke?
key_questions.looking_for: Smoking is a risk factor for stress incontinence and for bladder cancer

key_questions.question: How often do you have a bowel movement, and do you strain?
key_questions.looking_for: Chronic constipation and straining can worsen pelvic floor weakness and cause overflow leakage

key_questions.question: Does leaking urine stop you from work, exercise or social activities?
key_questions.looking_for: Assesses quality-of-life impact and guides treatment intensity

key_questions.question: Does anyone in your family have bladder control problems or did you wet the bed as a child?
key_questions.looking_for: Family history of incontinence or childhood bedwetting may suggest a hereditary or developmental contribution

reasoning_points: Characterizes the leakage pattern as stress, urge, overflow, functional or mixed based on triggers and timing
Identifies reversible or transient causes such as urinary tract infection, medications, constipation or hyperglycemia
Assesses for red flags including hematuria, neurologic deficits, fever and acute retention
Documents obstetric and surgical history relevant to pelvic floor and prostate function
Reviews medications and social factors such as caffeine, alcohol and smoking that worsen symptoms
Orders urinalysis and postvoid residual to distinguish overflow from stress or urge incontinence
Screens for diabetes and renal impairment as contributing or complicating conditions
Evaluates impact on quality of life to guide treatment
Considers look-alikes such as overactive bladder, benign prostatic hyperplasia, cauda equina syndrome and bladder cancer

easy: Older woman with classic stress leakage only with coughing, sneezing or lifting
Clear urge pattern with sudden urgency and leakage before reaching the toilet
Symptoms began after childbirth or menopause
No red flags and normal urinalysis
medium: Mixed stress and urge symptoms requiring careful history to separate components
Older man with dribbling and incomplete emptying suggesting overflow from benign prostatic hyperplasia
Patient on diuretics with worsening leakage
Urinalysis shows infection that must be treated before labeling chronic incontinence
hard: Older adult with functional incontinence from mobility or cognitive impairment
Patient with diabetes and both urge and overflow symptoms from neuropathy and incomplete emptying
New neurologic deficits or saddle anesthesia suggesting cauda equina syndrome
Hematuria in a smoker requiring evaluation for bladder cancer
Pregnancy-related stress leakage that may improve postpartum
